resources.string: Your mail goes only between this phone and your mail provider. No tracking, no ads.
Did you mean %1$s? If your address is correct, select Next again.
Enter a full email address, for example name@example.org.
Enter your address at riseup.net. You cannot sign in with an alias.
Enter a server name, for example mail.example.org.
Enter a server name, not an IP address. Plico cannot check the certificate of an IP address.
Find these settings on the help pages of your mail provider.
Plico found no server settings for this address. Enter them below.
Plico found these settings through DNS. Make sure that they are correct.
Keep this empty to use your email address.
Plico always uses encryption. It has no setting without encryption.
This provider needs an app password. Create one in the security settings of your account, then enter it here.
First, turn on IMAP access in the settings of your account.
For an address on your own domain, enter your iCloud Mail address (name@icloud.com) as the user name.
Sign in with your Riseup address and password. Plico connects only to mail.riseup.net.
Select how Plico signs in to your Google account.
Uses a Google account that is already on this phone.
Opens the Google sign-in page in your browser. Google can refuse this method for new OAuth clients. If this occurs, use an app password.
With an app password, Plico signs in without your Google password.
Turn on 2-Step Verification for your Google account.
Create an app password for Plico.
Use your own Google OAuth client
Shows the two Google sign-in methods. Plico has no client of its own.
Google lets an app use the Google sign-in only through an OAuth client. With your own client, your sign-in goes only between this phone and Google.
In the Google Cloud console, create a project.
Set up the OAuth consent screen. Select the user type External and the status In production. As the support email, use an address that is not personal: Google shows it on the sign-in page.
Create an OAuth client of the type Android with this package name and SHA-1 fingerprint:
Copy the client ID into the field below.
The client works only for this build of Plico, with the same package name and signing key.
This is not an OAuth client ID. A client ID ends with .apps.googleusercontent.com.
Outlook.com and Microsoft 365 accounts sign in through Microsoft in your browser.
In Outlook.com, go to Settings → Mail → Forwarding and IMAP. Turn on IMAP for devices and apps.
For this sign-in, Plico needs a Microsoft client ID that you own.
Opens the Microsoft sign-in page in your browser.
Shows the Microsoft sign-in. Plico has no client of its own.
Microsoft lets an app open a mailbox only through a registered client. With your own client, your sign-in goes only between this phone and Microsoft.
Open the Microsoft Entra admin center. You need a directory: a work account or a free Azure account.
Go to App registrations → New registration. For the account types, select \"Any Entra ID tenant and personal Microsoft accounts\".
Go to Authentication → Add a platform → Mobile and desktop applications. Add this redirect URI:
Copy the Application (client) ID into the field below.
A work or school account can need the approval of its administrator.
This is not a Microsoft client ID. A client ID has 32 hexadecimal digits in 5 groups, for example 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000.
Plico looks for the server settings…
Sign in to %1$s with your browser
Plico continues when the browser comes back to it.
The server did not accept the user name or the password. Make sure that both are correct.
Google needs an app password, not your Google password. Create an app password and enter it here.
Google did not accept the app password. Make sure that 2-Step Verification is on and that you copied the full app password.
%1$s did not accept the sign-in. Try again.
The account needs a change in its settings before Plico can use it.
Plico cannot connect to the server. Make sure that the phone is online, then try again.
The secure connection failed because the server certificate is not valid. A network that examines connections, for example at a hotel or at work, can cause this. Try again on a different network.
The server has too many connections now. Wait some minutes, then try again.
This account is already in Plico.
You signed in as %1$s. Sign in as %2$s.
Plico could not save the account. Try again.
%1$s does not let email apps connect with IMAP. Plico cannot add this account.
%1$s lets email apps connect only through its Bridge app on a computer. Plico cannot add this account.
The server did not start an encrypted connection. Plico does not connect without encryption. Make sure that the port and the security setting are correct.
These are the servers of %1$s. Remove this account and add it again.
One of these servers is a %1$s server. Use %1$s servers for incoming and outgoing mail.
Shown in Plico and in notifications.
Recipients see this name. You can leave it empty.
Plico downloads all messages. This can use much storage and data.
Plico keeps the messages of the last 30 days on this phone. It downloads older messages when you open them.
Gmail writes the public IP address of this phone into each message that you send. Recipients can see it. To hide it, use a VPN.
Plico keeps a connection to your mail server to show new mail immediately. For this, Android needs your permission.
Shows a notification when new mail arrives.
Lets Plico keep its connection while the phone sleeps. Plico wakes the phone only for new mail and for short connection checks.
Without background use, Plico needs exact alarms to check for mail at the correct time.
Create a new app password for %1$s and enter it here. Google cancels app passwords when you change your Google password.
This sign-in method needs your own %1$s client ID.
